summary: workflow status's --json/--agent output (newWorkflowStatusCmd, internal/cli/channel_workflow.go) now builds a structured envelope via workflowStatusEnvelope -- {store_status, resources: {<name>: {count, last_synced_at?}}, total, store_path, next_step (only when empty)} -- instead of json-encoding the bare Status() map, which serialized to "{}" on an empty store. store.LastSyncedTimes() (internal/store/store.go) is the new per-resource last-synced accessor this draws from, reading sync_state the same way internal/cli's existing sync-hint helpers already do. Any future regen touching this command must keep the empty-store case returning store_status "empty" plus a next_step, matching the shape the "search" MCP tool already uses for the same situation.
reason: Live-tested: workflow_status(plain=true) correctly said "No archived data. Run 'workflow archive' to sync.", but workflow_status(json=true) and workflow_status(agent=true) both returned a bare {}. The callers using --json/--agent are agents, so the mode that most needs a machine-readable answer was the one returning nothing actionable. search already returns {"count":0,"store_status":"empty",...} for the same situation, so workflow status should match that shape rather than leaving the JSON/agent case unfixed while plain-text worked.
validated_outcome: go build/vet/test/govulncheck and verify_skill.py all green. New tests: TestWorkflowStatusJSONReturnsStructuredEnvelopeWhenEmpty drives the real `workflow status --json` command against a never-synced store and asserts store_status="empty", an empty resources map, and a non-empty next_step (not a bare {}); TestWorkflowStatusJSONIncludesCountsAndLastSyncedAt archives real data first (reusing the existing fake-server harness from TestWorkflowArchiveActuallyArchivesData), then asserts store_status="ready", a workouts entry with count>0 and a non-empty last_synced_at, and a non-zero total.
